newsitem.title: UK: Stg fall does not always lead to price rises - BOE.
newsitem.headline: Stg fall does not always lead to price rises - BOE.

text.p: A sterling depreciation will not necessarily be associated with a rise in UK relative prices, the Bank of England said on Monday.

In a research paper contained in the Bank's quarterly bulletin, Mark Astley and Anthony Garratt of the Bank's monetary assessment and strategy division, said relative prices were actually more likely to fall if either aggregate supply or real spending developments underlied the depreciation.
But they were likely to rise if monetary developments underlie it. The relationship also holds in reverse if sterling appreciates, they said.

Evidence from econometric results using data going back to 1973 suggested that the relative consumer price responses to real spending and aggregate supply shocks are not significantly different from zero.
"The relative consumer price responses following monetary shocks are, however, significantly different from zero."

"So if a sterling exchange rate depreciation was caused by real spending or aggregate supply shocks -- which the results indicate was the case for most of sterling's movements between 1973 and 1994 -- it was unlikely to be associated with any significant change in UK relative prices," the paper said.
